Comments: Value=4 because Comoros has partially functional cross-border payment capability via PAPSS: Afreximbank reports BCC and PAPSS commenced implementation activities and that PAPSS "enables Comorians to make payments to other countries on the continent directly in Comorian francs," but also notes commercial banks still need to integrate/join for customers to benefit broadly.

Downgraded to Under development; flagged for human review given the conflict between the 2024 announcement and the 2026 coverage map.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: Value=5 because the Banque Centrale des Comores (BCC) directly operates core payment infrastructure (e.g., it "operates a cheque clearing house… SYCOCO") and is implementing ATS+ (RTGS/ACH/instant payments), while also having an explicit statutory mandate to ensure proper functioning/security of payment systems.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. BCC directly operates national payment infrastructure: it ran the SYCOCO cheque clearing house, launched the ATS+ interbank clearing system in 2025, and in May 2026 its Governor presented BCC-run systems (KomorPay, Komor Switch, Mali Ya Wakazi agent network, public securities market) built with in-house/local expertise. This is direct operation, not just regulation, consistent with the original score.

Comments: Value=3 because Comoros' personal data protection framework includes mandatory breach notification: Tech Hive Advisory reports controllers must notify the National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data within 72 hours (and notify data subjects where high risk).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Comoros' Personal Data Protection Law (2021) mandates 72-hour breach notification, corroborated by ConsentStack's regulatory summary and the primary legal text, in addition to the original Tech Hive Advisory source. Note: ConsentStack states the supervisory authority is not yet fully operational, so enforcement in practice may be limited, but the legal requirement itself is mandatory as scored.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Value=5 because Comoros has an operational nationwide interoperable digital payments infrastructure: PayLogic announced the "go-live of the National Payment Switch" connecting banks, microfinance institutions and mobile money operators and enabling "real-time… interoperable digital transactions" across the Union of Comoros.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised down. PayLogic's August 2025 vendor press release claimed a full 'go-live', but a World Bank project status report (May 2025) noted the switch was still piloting with 3 institutions with unresolved features (alias processing, instant payments, bill payments), and the central bank's own account of its May 2026 launch ceremony describes the Komor Switch rollout in three phases, with only Phase 1 (card-based ATM withdrawal nationwide) described as live and Phases 2-3 (instant bank-to-mobile-money transfer; merchant card/phone payment) still pending. Preferring the central bank's own, more recent account over the vendor's marketing claim, the system is best described as Partially deployed rather than Fully deployed nationwide.
